payload.title: [sfu-media-4] P2P maxParticipants=2 capability is never enforced — control plane lets unlimited users into a P2P...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING sfu-media-4 (medium/correctness, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/calls/call-control-plane.ts
LINES: 243-303, 343-399

WHAT: P2PWebRTCAdapter.describe() advertises maxParticipants:2 (p2p-media-plane.ts:110-112), and media-plane.ts documents this as the cap the control plane 'branches on'. But CallControlPlane never reads describe()/maxParticipants: createCall accepts any number of invitees and joinCall has no participant-count check against the media-plane capability (rg for maxParticipants in call-control-plane.ts and gateway.ts finds no enforcement). A creator can invite N users and all of them joinCall a P2P-brokered call.

IMPACT: For a P2P-configured deployment, the server issues join grants (TURN creds) to arbitrarily many participants for a topology that physically supports only 2. Clients negotiate a mesh the adapter never promised; control-plane state (participants/events) and TURN credential issuance scale unbounded while the documented invariant is violated. Capacity/abuse assumptions tied to maxParticipants are broken.

SUGGESTED FIX: In createCall/joinCall, consult mediaPlane.describe().maxParticipants and reject invitee lists / joins that would exceed it (e.g. throw a CallStateError before allocating/issuing tokens).
